S63.01.needs: a plan that can create schedules (otherwise the button reads Upgrade plan); at least one saved routine, because the gallery only shows when the list is not empty
S63.01.note: The Desktop app has the same gallery in apps/desktop/src/features/schedules/DesktopCloudSchedules.tsx, but its toggle button text was not confirmed.
steps: Sign in, click Scheduled in the sidebar.
Click the arrow button next to New task (aria-label "More ways to create a task").
Click Start from a template.
Look for the template gallery section titled Start from a template with ready-made routines to pick.
S63.01.where: Scheduled > More ways to create a task (arrow next to New task) > Start from a template

S63.02.needs: a plan that can create schedules
steps: Click Scheduled in the sidebar, then click New task.
Type a name in Schedule Name and the instructions in Task Instructions.
Pick a Frequency such as Daily, then click Create Schedule.
Look for the new routine card in the list with the name and prompt you typed.

S63.03.needs: a finished assistant reply in a chat
S63.03.note: The exact button that opens the reply's menu and whether the form is pre-filled from the reply were not confirmed in code.
steps: Send a message in chat and wait until the reply finishes streaming.
Open the menu on that reply.
Click Run this on a schedule.
Look for the schedule form opening, and check whether it carries that reply's content.
S63.03.where: Chat > a finished reply's menu > Run this on a schedule

S63.04.needs: a plan that can create schedules
S63.04.note: Edit Schedule is a tooltip title on an icon button, not visible text.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task.
Type a name in Schedule Name and text in Description.
Click Create Schedule, then click the Edit Schedule icon on the routine card.
Change the name or description, click Save Changes, and check the card shows the new values.
S63.04.where: Scheduled > New task > Schedule Name and Description (edit later with Scheduled > routine card > Edit Schedule)

S63.05.needs: a plan that can create schedules
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task.
Type several lines into Task Instructions, pressing Enter for new lines.
Click Create Schedule, then Edit Schedule on the card.
Look for the Task Instructions box showing all lines, edit one line, click Save Changes and check the change stays.
S63.05.where: Scheduled > New task > Task Instructions (later: routine card > Edit Schedule > Task Instructions)

S63.06.needs: a plan that can create schedules; a project with files if you want to test project files
S63.06.note: The Code line pointed to moved lines. The Sources group was found in ScheduleAccessFields.tsx; I did not confirm that the form renders it.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task.
Find the Sources group of checkboxes.
Tick or untick Project instructions and files, Saved memories, The web or Recent chats.
Click Create Schedule, reopen Edit Schedule, and check the same boxes are still set.

S63.08.needs: a plan that can create schedules; connectors set up in the account to see choices
S63.08.note: Whether the list is empty without connectors was not confirmed.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task.
Find the Connectors group; wait for Reading your connectors to go away.
Tick the connectors the routine may use.
Click Create Schedule, reopen Edit Schedule and check the choice is kept.

S63.09.needs: a plan that can create schedules; at least one custom agent created to see choices beyond No agent
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task.
Open the Run as agent drop-down; the default is No agent.
Pick an agent from the list.
Click Create Schedule and check the card or Edit Schedule shows that agent.
S63.09.where: Scheduled > New task > Run as agent

steps: Click Scheduled, then New task.
Set Frequency to One Time.
Pick a date and time in Run At that is in the future.
Click Create Schedule and check the card shows that one time as its next run.
S63.11.where: Scheduled > New task > Frequency > One Time > Run At

S63.12.note: Whether the card shows the repeat wording was not confirmed.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task.
Set Frequency to Daily, then set Local Time.
Click Create Schedule.
Look at the card's next-run information and check it repeats at the chosen time.
S63.12.where: Scheduled > New task > Frequency > Daily, Weekly or Monthly

S63.13.note: The Code line pointed to moved lines; the field was found at ScheduleForm.tsx line 510.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task.
Click the Time Zone field and type a city or region in Search by city or region…
Pick a zone, then set a Local Time.
Click Create Schedule, reopen Edit Schedule and check the Time Zone is kept.
Click Scheduled, then New task.
Set Frequency to Interval and fill Repeat Every, or Custom Cron and fill Cron Expression, or Recurrence Rule and fill Recurrence Rule.
Optionally set Only Run During to a window.
Click Create Schedule and check the card shows the advanced recurrence.
S63.14.where: Scheduled > New task > Frequency > Interval, Custom Cron or Recurrence Rule

S63.15.needs: a connected account for the chosen service (for example GitHub or Gmail) to test a real event
S63.15.note: Not confirmed whether the trigger panel is inside the form or appears after saving; firing an event was not verified in code.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task.
Set Frequency to When An Event Happens.
Look for the trigger choices: GitHub, Slack, Gmail, Google Calendar, Anything else (signed webhook).
Pick one, save, then send or cause that event and check a run starts.
S63.15.where: Scheduled > New task > Frequency > When An Event Happens

S63.16.needs: a connected event source to send real events
S63.16.note: Only the field conditions were confirmed; event type, account and repeat-suppression wording was not found as visible labels.
steps: Set Frequency to When An Event Happens and pick a trigger.
Find the Only when group.
Pick a field from the drop-down, or Other field…, and enter a Value.
Save, send a matching and a non-matching event, and check only the matching one starts a run.
S63.16.where: Scheduled > New task > Frequency > When An Event Happens > Only when

S63.17.needs: a terminal to send the POST; the signing secret from the panel
S63.17.note: The panel builds a signed curl example; the exact labels for the URL and secret were not confirmed.
steps: Set Frequency to When An Event Happens and pick Anything else (signed webhook).
Save, then copy the endpoint and signing secret shown in the trigger panel.
Send a signed POST to the endpoint, using the example command shown in the panel.
Look in the routine's run history for a new run.
S63.17.where: Scheduled > New task > Frequency > When An Event Happens > Anything else (signed webhook)

S63.19.needs: a saved routine; a routine that is finished or legacy shows Run now disabled
S63.19.note: The button that opens the card menu was not confirmed in code.
steps: Click Scheduled and open the menu on a saved routine.
Click Run now.
Look for a new run in Latest result or the run history with a status and output.
S63.19.where: Scheduled > routine card menu > Run now

S63.20.note: The label used on the card itself was not confirmed; Next run found here is the sort option text.
steps: Click Scheduled and look at each routine card.
Find the next-run time (shown as a tooltip titled Next run on the card).
Compare the time with the Time Zone and Local Time set in Edit Schedule.

S63.21.needs: a routine that has run at least once; a failing run to see the error
steps: Click Scheduled and open a routine that has run.
Look for the Last run line on its card.
If the last run failed, check the error text after Last run.

labels.text: This schedule has not run yet.

S63.22.note: The control that opens Latest result from the card was not confirmed in code.
steps: Click Scheduled and open a routine that has run.
Open the Latest result panel from the card.
Look for the list of past runs with status and time.
If there are no runs, check the text This schedule has not run yet.
S63.22.where: Scheduled > routine card > Latest result (run history)

S63.23.needs: a routine with a finished run that produced output
S63.23.note: Opening a single run and its output view was not confirmed in code; ScheduleRunHistory.tsx shows the run list.
steps: Open Latest result for a routine that has run.
Click or open a past run in the list.
Look for the run's output text, not only its status.
S63.23.where: Scheduled > routine card > Latest result > a run

steps: Click Scheduled and find a routine that is active.
Click Pause on its card, or Pause in the card menu.
Look for the Paused label on the card and that it does not run at its next time.
Click Resume and check the label goes away.

S63.26.note: Edit Schedule is a tooltip title on an icon button.
steps: Click Scheduled and click the Edit Schedule icon on a routine card.
Change a field such as Frequency, Local Time or Task Instructions.
Click Save Changes.
Look at the card and reopen Edit Schedule to check the change saved.

S63.27.needs: a saved routine; the deletion is permanent
S63.27.note: The card menu that holds Delete was not confirmed in code; the dialog wording was read but its consequence text was not.
steps: Click Scheduled and open the menu on a routine.
Click Delete.
Read the confirmation Delete Schedule? and confirm.
Look for the routine gone from the list and that it no longer runs.

S63.29.needs: a second account to open the link
S63.29.note: The Share menu item wording was taken from a test file, not the component; the recipient copy flow was not confirmed.
steps: Click Scheduled and open the share action for a routine.
In the dialog, copy the Share link.
Open the link in a second account in the same workspace or another browser, and check it offers to create a copy.
Check the original routine is unchanged.
S63.29.where: Scheduled > routine card > Share (link dialog Share “<routine name>”)

S63.31.needs: a plan that can create schedules
S63.31.note: Empty fields show the placeholder No limit…; whether all plans can set these was not confirmed.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task.
Fill Maximum Runs with a number, and optionally Credit Cap.
Click Create Schedule.
Let the routine reach the limit, or check Edit Schedule shows the cap is kept.
S63.31.where: Scheduled > New task > Maximum Runs and Credit Cap

S63.32.needs: a routine whose unattended run needs a tool approval (the tool's approval has to be triggered by the run)
S63.32.note: The approve and deny button words come from TOOL_APPROVAL_ACTION_LABELS in packages/types, not a literal in these files. The desktop screen (apps/desktop/src/features/schedules/DesktopCloudSchedules.tsx) shows the same approval box under "Recent results" and asks the user to approve in run history. The code paths for pausing and resuming are in apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts and the tool-call gate; the resume after approval was not confirmed on screen, and the labels for the "resume the schedule" action were not checked.
steps: Sign in and open "Scheduled" in the left sidebar.
Open a routine that uses a tool which asks for approval, and run it unattended (or wait for its schedule to fire).
When the run needs approval, the routine card shows a paused note: "Paused: a run needed your approval. Approve or deny it in Run History". Click the Run History (clock) icon on the card.
In the run row, look for the "Waiting for your approval" box listing the tool calls with an approve and a deny button, and an "Expires" time.
Click approve. Compare with Expected: the run should resume and finish, and the approval box should go away.
S63.32.where: Scheduled > (routine card) > Run History (clock icon) > run row shows "Waiting for your approval" with the approve and deny buttons

S63.33.needs: a routine with a recurring schedule and a run that was actually missed (the tester cannot force this easily)
S63.33.note: The note text is built in code (a template string), so the full sentence is not one literal; the setting label "If A Run Is Missed" is in apps/web/features/schedules/components/ScheduleForm.tsx. The desktop Recent results section (apps/desktop/src/features/schedules/DesktopCloudSchedules.tsx) also shows the same timing note. Whether a missed run is shown in a live test was not verified.
steps: Sign in and open "Scheduled" in the left sidebar.

Make sure a routine has a recurring schedule and its run was missed (for example the computer was asleep or the app was closed when it was due). The "If A Run Is Missed" setting in the routine form decides whether it runs late or is skipped.
Click the Run History (clock) icon on the routine card.
Read the run row: a skipped run shows the word "skipped" in place of the status, plus a note explaining why. A late run shows the note "Ran late: scheduled for ...".
Compare with Expected: the history should say that the occurrence was missed or skipped and why.
S63.33.where: Scheduled > (routine card) > Run History (clock icon) > run row shows "skipped" and a note such as "Skipped the run scheduled for ..." or "Ran late: scheduled for ..."
